name.en: Fake toll text: “pay your overdue toll now”

how.en: A text says you owe an overdue toll and copies a real toll program such as E-ZPass, SunPass, FasTrak or TxTag. It threatens late fees or suspension of your vehicle registration if you don’t pay right away, and links to a fake payment page that takes your card details. The FTC says these messages helped push reports of government imposter scams up 40% in 2025.

text.en: A text claims to be from a toll program you know.
It says you have an unpaid toll and threatens fees or a suspended registration.
It links to a page to pay.
The page takes your card details.
E-ZPass: Our records show an unpaid toll of $6.85 on your account. Pay by tomorrow to avoid a $50 late fee and registration hold: [link]

en: A text about a toll with a link to pay.
Threats of late fees or a suspended registration if you don’t pay now.
A small amount meant to make you pay without checking.
Don’t tap the link. Contact your state’s toll agency using a number or website you know is real.
If you entered card details, call your card issuer.
